[package]
name = "formal-ai"
version = "0.355.14"
edition = "2024"
description = "Don't know everything, know just enough to get to know anything"
readme = "../README.md"
license = "Unlicense"
keywords = ["formal-ai", "symbolic-ai", "openai", "links"]
categories = ["command-line-utilities", "web-programming::http-server"]
repository = "https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai"
documentation = "https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai"
rust-version = "1.99"
include = [
    "/Cargo.lock",
    "/Cargo.toml",
    "../LICENSE",
    "../README.md",
    "/build.rs",
    "/embedded/**",
    "/src/**",
]
build = "build.rs"

# docs.rs sets DOCS_RS while building dependencies. meta-language currently
# pulls lindera-jieba, whose DOCS_RS build path is broken upstream
# (lindera/lindera#750). Keep the complete engine enabled for every normal build,
# while letting docs.rs render this crate's API without executing that transitive
# build script.
[package.metadata.docs.rs]
no-default-features = true

# Issue #1181: the `cli` job of the Desktop Release workflow publishes
# prebuilt standalone archives as release assets, so `cargo binstall
# formal-ai` downloads one of those instead of compiling this crate. The
# archives hold `formal-ai-cli-<triple>/{formal-ai,LICENSE,README.md}`; names
# are version-less because each GitHub release namespaces its own assets.
[package.metadata.binstall]
pkg-url = "{ repo }/releases/download/v{ version }/formal-ai-cli-{ target }.tar.gz"
pkg-fmt = "tgz"
bin-dir = "formal-ai-cli-{ target }/{ bin }{ binary-ext }"

[package.metadata.binstall.overrides.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]
pkg-url = "{ repo }/releases/download/v{ version }/formal-ai-cli-{ target }.zip"
pkg-fmt = "zip"

[lib]
name = "formal_ai"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "formal-ai"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
base64 = "0.23"
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "env"] }
command-stream = "1.5"
egg = { version = "0.11.0", default-features = false, features = ["deterministic"], optional = true }
lino-arguments = "0.4.0"
lino-objects-codec = "0.8.0"
links-notation = "0.23.0"
link-calculator = "0.22.0"
# CST/AST engine: the link-foundation meta-language links network. It ships
# real tree-sitter grammars for every language we target and exposes a single
# mutable links-network representation, so it is the sole CST/AST engine here
# (https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language).
meta-language = { version = "1.0.0", optional = true }
nom = "8"
kamadak-exif = "0.6.1"
regex = "1"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = { version = "1", features = ["float_roundtrip"] }
sha2 = "0.11"
shell-words = "1.1.1"
fs2 = "0.4"
thread-priority = "3.1.1"
toml_edit = "0.25.15"
tokio = { version = "1.53.3", features = ["rt", "time"] }
# General categories for the lib's word segmentation: abugida conjuncts are
# held together by combining marks, which `char::is_alphanumeric` excludes.
unicode-general-category = "1.1"
walkdir = "2"
which = "8"
unicode-normalization = "0.1"
# URL Standard observer shared with JavaScript's URL API; already present in Cargo.lock.
url = "2.5.8"

[target.'cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))'.dependencies]
tokio = { version = "1.53.3", features = ["process", "io-util", "signal"] }
blake3 = { version = "1.8.7", features = ["rayon"] }
ring = "0.17"
tracing = "0.1.44"
wgpu = { version = "30.0.1", optional = true }
pollster = { version = "0.4.0", optional = true }
async-trait = "0.1"
bytes = "1"
link-cli = { version = "1.0.0", optional = true }
tungstenite = "0.30"
web-capture = { version = "0.3.37", default-features = false, features = ["search"] }
web-search = { version = "0.6.0", default-features = false, features = ["merge"] }
webrtc = "0.21"

[features]
provenance-gpu = ["dep:wgpu", "dep:pollster"]
default = ["doublets-native", "equality-saturation", "meta-language"]
doublets-native = ["dep:link-cli"]
equality-saturation = ["dep:egg"]
meta-language = ["dep:meta-language"]

[dev-dependencies]
# The same codec the library encodes with, so tests can hold published
# artifacts to the notation they claim to be written in.
lino-objects-codec = "0.8.0"
temp-env = "0.3.6"

[lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"

[lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
nursery = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }

# Allow some common patterns
module_name_repetitions = "allow"
too_many_lines = "allow"
missing_errors_doc = "allow"
missing_panics_doc = "allow"

[[test]]
name = "unit"
path = "tests/unit/mod.rs"

[[test]]
name = "integration"
path = "tests/integration/mod.rs"

[[test]]
name = "source"
path = "tests/source/mod.rs"

# This crate embeds large language dictionaries and compiles dozens of parser
# grammars. Cargo's defaults retain full debuginfo plus incremental state for
# every test/example binary, which made ordinary development workspaces grow
# past 10 GiB. Keep fast debug assertions, but do not retain those two largest
# classes of recomputable artifacts. Developers who need debugger symbols can
# opt in with `CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=2` for that run.
[profile.dev]
debug = 0
incremental = false

[profile.test]
debug = 0
incremental = false
# Issue #1053: the slow tests here are pure in-process computation -- the seven
# that exceed 60s spawn no subprocesses at all -- so running them unoptimized
# spends most of their time in code the compiler would have folded away.
# Measured on `installation_conversion::popular_github_projects_route_through_
# install_conversion`: 52.86s at opt-level 0 against 9.34s at 2, a 5.7x
# difference, for +40s of one-time compilation per job.
#
# `debug-assertions` and `overflow-checks` stay on deliberately. They are
# independent of `opt-level`, and turning them off would change what the tests
# actually check: `debug_assert!` appears in `src/` and an arithmetic overflow
# must keep panicking here rather than wrapping silently.
opt-level = 2
debug-assertions = true
overflow-checks = true

[profile.release]
# Issue #1055: no LTO, and no cap on codegen units.
#
# Link-time optimization is the one stage of a Rust build that does not
# parallelize: it merges every crate into a single optimization unit and links
# it on one thread, so more cores do not shorten it. Measured here on
# `cargo test --release --no-run --bins --tests` from a touched `lib.rs`:
#
#   lto = true,  codegen-units = 1    867s
#   lto = false, codegen-units unset  162s
#
# 705 seconds, 5.4x, sitting on the critical path of everything downstream --
# tests, packaging, Docker, the release chain. Issue #1043 had already measured
# the same effect on one job (536s -> 372s) and dropped LTO there; this applies
# the finding everywhere rather than one job at a time.
#
# `codegen-units` is left at the default so the compiler splits the work across
# every core the runner has. Pinning it to 1 was what forbade that.
#
# The cost is a slightly slower binary at runtime. Nothing in this pipeline
# measures that, and no benchmark gates on it; the build time it buys back is
# measured and immediate.
lto = false
strip = true

# Safe no-follow/identity adapters reuse already-locked audited platform crates.
[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
rustix = { version = "1.1.5", features = ["fs", "process"] }

[target.'cfg(windows)'.dependencies]
winapi-util = "0.1.11"
windows-sys = { version = "0.61.2", features = ["Win32_Storage_FileSystem"] }
